subject: MAP Draft — Technical evaluation milestones, targets, and owners
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP Draft — Technical evaluation milestones & responsibilities

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) template, I captured the technical-eval milestone slate and proposed owners below. Please review and confirm where you want ownership to sit on your side, and whether the suggested target close date looks realistic with your procurement cadence.

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (Redwood / HealthGrid)
1) Sandbox access & service account (HealthGrid)
   - Description: Provide sandbox API key, example payloads, and short-lived SSH/VPC access (if needed) for performance tests.
   - Owner: Alyssa Turner (HealthGrid)
   - Target due: 2026-08-25

2) Benchmark dataset & success criteria (joint)
   - Description: HealthGrid to share a PII-sanitized sample subset; Redwood to run benchmark harness and return results.
   - Success criteria (pass = all must be met):
     * Semantic accuracy: intent/extraction F1 >= 0.88 across defined scenarios
     * Hallucination: < 3% on injected factual checks
     * Latency: 99th percentile <= 250 ms for 2k-token requests under steady-state (see note on concurrency below)
     * Cost: average token cost <= $0.0008 per token for production config
   - Owner: joint (HealthGrid provides dataset; Redwood runs tests)
   - Target due: 2026-08-31

3) Model shortlist & quantization profile (Redwood)
   - Description: Redwood proposes a slate of model variants to test (baseline & lower-cost quantized choices).
   - Initial shortlist: Llama2-Chat-70B (Q8), Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8), Falcon-40B-instruct (Q4_0)
   - Owner: Redwood (Ben / Soojin)
   - Target due: 2026-08-24

4) Throughput and routing policy validation (Redwood + HealthGrid)
   - Description: Validate autoscaling and fallback routing for cross-region traffic and burst scenarios.
   - Owner: Redwood infra + HealthGrid infra contact (TBD)
   - Target due: 2026-09-03

Dependencies & open items
- HealthGrid to share sanitized evaluation subset (PII removed) and a small set of acceptance prompts.
- Confirm sequence length distribution and expected concurrency (see Ben's follow-up for specifics).
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned aiming for a live contract by ~Sep 10 — please flag if that slips.

Attachments: redwood-map-draft-v1.pdf (MAP with milestones and MSA/POC checklist).

Next steps
- Alyssa: confirm sandbox credentials timeline + upload sanitized subset (target Aug 25).
- Ben/Redwood: produce benchmark instructions and baseline run plan by Aug 24.
- I’ll update the MAP with confirmed owners and share an SOW draft if timelines hold.

Thanks — will follow up after Ben’s note with the harness specifics.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0197
[Attachment: redwood-map-draft-v1.pdf]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Draft — Technical evaluation milestones & responsibilities

Adding the technical runbook details so we’re all aligned on inputs we need from HealthGrid and the metrics we’ll produce. High level — Redwood will run the harness in your sandbox (or our private test env with mirrored traffic) and provide the raw logs + condensed report.

What we need from HealthGrid (minimum):
- Sample CSV (PII-filtered) of ~1k rows covering the top 10 intent buckets and edge cases. Thanks for offering this — ideal to get it by 2026-08-25.
- Typical sequence length distribution (percentile breakdown: 50th/90th/99th) and an example payload for chat vs. single-turn generation.
- Concurrency targets: baseline steady-state 20 RPS, burst 100 RPS for ~30s. If you expect higher sustained RPS, flag that now.
- Any mandatory redaction rules or tokenization quirks we should apply before testing.

What Redwood will deliver:
- Baseline latency & throughput report (p50/p95/p99) for each model variant, measured under the stated concurrency profile.
- Cost estimate per request and per token for the tested config using our batching and quantization profiles.
- Failure modes and fallback suggestions (e.g., lower-cost model variants for fallback routing).
- Repro steps + script (benchmark-instructions.md) and raw logs (sanitized).

Notes on models & configs:
- We recommend starting with the three variants in Karthik’s note. For cost-constrained runs we’ll include an int8 quantized run of Mistral-Instruct-7B.
- For latency fairness, we’ll pin sequence-length at the 90th percentile reported in your distribution.

Attachments: benchmark-instructions.md (short how-to), sample JMeter profile (stub).

Small ask: can HealthGrid confirm whether sandbox traffic should route through your VPC peering or if you prefer Redwood-hosted test harness? The VPC path lets us validate real network egress behavior (relevant for your SLA).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: benchmark-instructions.md]
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 18:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MAP Draft — Technical evaluation milestones & responsibilities

Thanks — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Quick confirmations: 
- We can deliver a PII-sanitized subset by COB 2026-08-25 (see attached CSV). [Attachment: healthgrid_eval_subset.csv]
- Baseline concurrency expectation is ~25 RPS steady, with spikes to ~120 RPS for ~1 minute during peak test windows — so please size the burst to 120 RPS.
- Sequence length percentiles (approx): p50=512 tokens, p90=1,950 tokens, p99=2,700 tokens. Hope that helps your latency planning.
- Procurement: our internal stakeholder timeline is aggressive; procurement will aim for execution by 2026-09-10 but finance needs the SOW and an initial MSA redline first.

We’re available for a short working call on Mon Aug 24 at 10:00 AM PT if that works for Redwood to walk through dataset specifics and access method. Let me know and I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Alyssa Turner
Director, Product Integrations — HealthGrid
alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com | +1 (617) 555-1234
[Attachment: healthgrid_eval_subset.csv (sanitized sample)]

Subject: Re: MAP Draft — Technical evaluation milestones & responsibilities

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround and the percentile numbers, Alyssa. We’ll adjust the MAP targets to reflect p99 sequence lengths and size the burst to 120 RPS.

Ben: please update the benchmark run plan to use p90/p99 seq lengths Alyssa provided and include a burst test at 120 RPS. I’ll send an updated MAP + a one-page SOW draft by tomorrow morning for HealthGrid review (procurement input).

Alyssa: please go ahead and send the calendar invite for Aug 24 10:00 AM PT. We’ll have Ben and Soojin on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the harness running.

—
